_comment: The MCU no-heap link check's ratchet (tools/check_no_heap.py, #1783, ADR-0083 Decision 1).
Per target, every function (one section, with -ffunction-sections) that reaches the heap:
{object: {section: {entry point or 'via <callee>': count}}}. A function reaches the heap by
naming an entry point or by calling, within libtracer.a, one that does (to a fixpoint). A pin
may only be lowered (--repin); a function not pinned here, or one that gained a path or a
count, fails CI. Empty targets are the goal. Most pins are deleting destructors and std
containers not yet on the seam, and everything that calls them; the PR for #1783 lists them.

One-time exception (#2022 slice 1, PR #2077): 14 esp32c6 pins were ADDED by hand, none a new heap call; every added edge ends at a function already pinned on main, directly or through a new destructor stub/lambda thunk: 7 calls the closure could not see through a vtable before (make_poly's recorded ~X for tcp, tcp_server, can, tcp session; send(span)->send(iov) devirtualized by final x3), 4 address references to those thunks, and main's 2 invoke_impl->ctor edges now appear as 3 entries after the factory lambda went out of line. Not a precedent: every other change to this file only lowers pins.

#1951 (PR #2050, delete COMPACT) re-seeded esp32c6 after inlining moved: 2 new sections and 14 grown edges only re-attribute paths to callees already pinned (remote_ptr_t::free_record, value_t::destroy, rope_t::append absorbing vector::reserve); no new heap entry point, and the target drops 1884 -> 1836 references.

#1606 (PR #2128, lazy client-link construction) re-pinned esp_ws_client_link.cpp.obj by hand: the recv thread is now spawned in start_receiving() instead of the constructor, so the three std::thread instantiations for the ctor lambda (thread ctor, _State_impl::_M_run, ~_State_impl) are renamed to start_receiving's lambda with identical keys and counts, the ctor's 'via thread' x2 moved to start_receiving, and the ctor reaches it once. Same heap reachability moved to the lazy arm path, no new entry point; the target stays at 1836 references.

#2143 (PR #2201, copy-or-share trait) re-seeded esp32c6 from main by renames only: share_or_copy_tlv<arena_node/view_node> takes a share_hint_t where it took an unsigned store_ref_min_bytes, so 14 keys (26 references) in op_resolve.cpp.obj and op_resolve_view.cpp.obj change their mangled names with identical callees and counts. No new heap entry point and no reference over main.

#1622 (PR #2099, store the subscriber table once) re-seeded graph.cpp.obj and graph_fields.cpp.obj from the real esp32c6 build. The slot table element type is renamed (block_array_t<subscriber_t> -> block_array_t<subscriber_slot_t>; the retire batch block_array_t<block_array_t<subscriber_t>> -> block_array_t<detached_edges_t>), which the rename pass cannot pair across template arguments. Both new types are mem::bitwise_relocatable, so their growth (regrow, relocate, grow_emplace) reaches no destructor and no longer reaches the heap at all: total references 1944 -> 1936 on main after #2143 (measured on the head rebased onto ef6977d6), direct heap calls unchanged, every other object identical, and every new edge ends at a function already pinned on main (segment_ptr_t::reset, view_t::operator=, remote_ptr_t::free_record, scan_retired_edges). Not a precedent.
#2238 (PR #2243, +1 pin approved by the maintainer 2026-10-22): makes the previously virtual-hidden retained-send edge explicit; goes with the self-heal worker (#1792/#2147).

#2244 (delete the RFC-0027 path-label plane, RFC-0029 S3) re-seeded cortex-m0 path.o and esp32c6 fwd_router/op_resolve/op_resolve_view/path/transport_vertex objects from the real builds: the deleted functions (path_t::cache_path_label, fwd_router_t::adopt_path_label) leave, resolve_node loses two parameters (renamed sections, resolve_node<view_node> now inlined into its caller), and path_t's one fewer std::vector lets GCC inline ~_Vector_base into ~path_t (one more direct operator delete there, the inlined body of a call already pinned). On esp32c6, path_t::parse's three operator new calls via _M_allocate likewise become direct (1 -> 4). No new heap entry point; cortex-m0 drops 36 -> 32 references, esp32c6 1938 -> 1930.
